# `silk/io/writer`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The `Writer` effect: write bytes without knowing where they go.

## When to use
Require `&mut Writer` in a function that writes output, such as text for a person or a file
format. The caller decides where the bytes go when it provides the writer. Use
`silk.text.format.Format` to write values as text. Use `silk.io.logger.Logger` for log events.

## Details
A function that needs a writer has `? &mut Writer` in its type. The caller supplies a provider
with `Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut provider)`. A provider is any type that implements
[`Writer.writeAll`](#Writer.writeAll) and [`Writer.flush`](#Writer.flush), and optionally [`Writer.writeVectored`](#Writer.writeVectored).
`silk.io.writer_native` has `StdoutWriter` and `StderrWriter`. `silk.io.buffered_output` collects small
writes into larger ones. A test can provide a writer that keeps the bytes in memory.

[`Writer.writeVectored`](#Writer.writeVectored) writes several slices as one. A provider with no faster way to do it
leaves it out and gets the default, one `writeAll` for each slice.

## Errors
- [`WriterError`](#WriterError) if the provider cannot complete a write or a flush. Bytes that the provider
  accepted before the failure stay written.

## Gotchas
The providers in `silk.io.writer_native` exist on Windows x86_64 MSVC without a CRT, WASI,
Darwin x86_64 or aarch64, and Linux x86_64 or aarch64 with GNU libc. Windows consoles require complete
canonical WTF-8 per write or concatenated vectored write; redirected handles accept arbitrary bytes.

## Examples
### Write to a provider that counts bytes
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }

struct CountingWriter {
  count: usize,
}

impl Writer for CountingWriter {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, value: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    self.count = self.count + value.length
    return ()
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    return ()
  }
}

effect fn greet() -> ()
  ! WriterError
  ? &mut Writer {
  run Writer.writeString("Hello, ")
  run Writer.writeString("world\n")
  return run Writer.flush()
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! WriterError {
  let mut writer = CountingWriter { count: 0 }
  run greet() |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut writer)
  if writer.count != 13 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## See also
- `silk.text.format` to write numbers, strings, and templates.
- `silk.io.buffered_output` to make fewer, larger writes.

<a id="Writer"></a>

## `Writer`

```silk
pub service Writer
```

The effect that receives output bytes, without the writer knowing where they go.

### When to use

Require `&mut Writer` in a function that writes output, such as text for a person or a file
format. The caller decides where the bytes go when it provides the writer, with
`Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut provider)`. Use `silk.text.format.Format` to write values as text,
and `silk.io.logger.Logger` for log events. `silk.io.writer_native` has `StdoutWriter` and
`StderrWriter`, and `silk.io.buffered_output` collects small writes into larger ones.

### Details

A provider implements [`Writer.writeAll`](#Writer.writeAll) and [`Writer.flush`](#Writer.flush), and optionally
[`Writer.writeVectored`](#Writer.writeVectored).
Code that writes calls them through the effect, as `run Writer.writeAll(bytes)`, and does not
know which provider it uses. A provider with no faster way to write several slices leaves
`writeVectored` out and gets the default, one `writeAll` for each slice.

<a id="Writer.writeAll"></a>

### Operation `writeAll`

```silk
effect fn writeAll(val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes all of `val`. It returns only after the provider accepted every byte or failed.

#### Errors

- [`WriterError`](#WriterError) if the provider fails. Some bytes can be written before the failure.

<a id="Writer.writeVectored"></a>

### Operation `writeVectored`

```silk
effect fn writeVectored(vals: &[&[u8]]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes all bytes of each slice of `vals`, in order, as if they were one slice.

#### When to use

Use `writeVectored` for a message that is in several parts, such as a header and a body,
without first copying the parts together.

#### Details

A provider can send all parts in one operation, such as one `writev` system call. A provider
with no such operation leaves it out, and this default calls `writeAll` once for each part.
Empty slices write nothing.

#### Errors

- [`WriterError`](#WriterError) if the provider fails. Some bytes can be written before the failure.

<a id="Writer.flush"></a>

### Operation `flush`

```silk
effect fn flush() -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Asks the provider to send any bytes that it holds in a buffer to their destination.

#### Errors

- [`WriterError`](#WriterError) if the provider cannot send the bytes.

<a id="Writer.impl.failure"></a>

### Associated function `failure`

```silk
pub fn failure() -> WriterError
```

Returns a [`WriterError`](#WriterError). A provider returns it when a write or a flush fails.

<a id="Writer.impl.ignoreError"></a>

### Method `ignoreError`

```silk
pub effect fn ignoreError<A, E, ?R>(self: once Effect<A ! E ? R>) -> A | () ? R
```

Runs `self` and returns its value. If it fails, returns `()` and drops the error.

#### When to use

Use `ignoreError` for output where a failure does not matter, such as a diagnostic message in
a program that is about to exit.

#### Gotchas

The error is lost. The result type is `A | ()`, so the caller cannot tell a failure from a
successful `()`.

<a id="Writer.impl.writeString"></a>

### Associated function `writeString`


Writes the UTF-8 bytes of `val`.

#### Errors

- [`WriterError`](#WriterError) if the provider fails. Some bytes can be written before the failure.
